discovery: In situ resolution of the electron-scale physics of magnetic reconnection in space plasmas

nominees.name: James L. Burch
nominees.affiliation: Southwest Research Institute, San Antonio, USA

nominees.name: Tai D. Phan
nominees.affiliation: Space Sciences Laboratory, University of California, Berkeley, USA

motivation: Magnetic reconnection converts magnetic energy into particle energy throughout the universe: in solar flares, in magnetospheric substorms, in fusion devices and in astrophysical jets. For decades its central mechanism, how field lines break inside the tiny electron diffusion region, was accessible only to theory. Michael Hesse's kinetic theory and simulations identified the non-gyrotropic electron pressure as the agent that breaks the frozen-in condition. James Burch conceived and led the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission, whose four spacecraft flew through electron diffusion regions at Earth's magnetopause and in the magnetotail and measured the predicted crescent-shaped electron distributions and energy conversion directly. Tai Phan's observations established reconnection in the solar wind and discovered electron-only reconnection in turbulent plasma. Together they turned a basic plasma process into an experimentally verified, predictive physics that underlies space weather forecasting and the protection of satellites.
